questions.q: Which install method updates Power BI Desktop automatically and doesn't require admin rights?
options: Only the Report Server version updates automatically
questions.explain: The Microsoft Store version downloads monthly updates in the background and doesn't require administrator privileges to install.

questions.q: Why would an organization choose the direct .exe download over the Microsoft Store version?
options: Because it has more features than the Store version
Because it doesn't require the latest version of Windows
To silently script the install across many machines with command-line switches
questions.explain: Both methods install the same free, fully-featured version. The .exe supports command-line switches like -quiet and ACCEPT_EULA=1 for IT-managed, scripted rollouts.

questions.q: Which version of the direct download should you choose?
questions.explain: The 32-bit version of Power BI Desktop is no longer supported. Always install the 64-bit version.

questions.q: What is the minimum display resolution Power BI Desktop requires?
questions.explain: Lower resolutions like 1024x768 or 1280x800 aren't supported — some dialogs and controls render beyond what fits on screen below 1440x900/1600x900.

questions.q: If Power BI Desktop renders with large black areas after launching, what's the most likely cause and fix?
options: A corrupted install that requires reinstalling
A missing Power BI Pro license
A Windows display-scaling issue — use "Let Windows fix apps that are blurry"
questions.explain: This is a known Windows rendering issue tied to display scaling, not a Power BI defect. Windows' built-in "fix apps that are blurry" option resolves it.
